capability.summary: Parse one UTF-8 YAML document and return its JSON-compatible value
capability.description: Reads one local UTF-8 file, parses exactly one YAML document with PyYAML safe_load, and emits the resulting Python value under a `json` field in a JSON envelope. It does not write a converted file, and safe YAML values that are not JSON-serializable can still fail during envelope emission.
capability.problem_space: Single-document YAML parsing for JSON-compatible configuration/data values. It is not multi-document streaming, schema validation, YAML linting, round-trip formatting, comment/style preservation, JSON-to-YAML conversion, or a filesystem JSON exporter.

constraint.io_signature: Input: required file_path string at CLI position 1 naming an existing UTF-8 YAML file containing one document. Output: JSON envelope with the safe_load value in `json`; no `.json` file is written.
accepted_inputs: an existing UTF-8 YAML file containing exactly one PyYAML-safe document whose constructed value is JSON-serializable
constraint.output_shape: Success JSON envelope: {status: "success", tool: "PyYAML", target: string, json: any JSON-compatible value}, exit 0; an empty document or YAML null produces json=null. The outer envelope is emitted by json.dumps with default allow_nan=true, so a payload containing YAML NaN/Infinity may be non-strict RFC JSON; non-string YAML mapping keys are stringified and can collide. Non-existing path: {status: "error", message: string}, exit 2. PyYAML YAMLError, including malformed or multiple-document input rejected by safe_load: {status: "error", tool: "PyYAML", message: "invalid YAML: <details>"}, exit 1. Missing argument prints usage to stderr and exits 1 without JSON. File/UTF-8 errors and JSON serialization failures are uncaught and may traceback.
limitations: safe_load reads and materializes the complete YAML document before json.dumps emits the envelope; input and result sizes are unbounded and nested data can amplify memory use
the wrapper's json.dumps uses the default allow_nan=true behavior, so YAML NaN/Infinity values may be emitted as NaN/Infinity rather than strict RFC JSON
JSON emission stringifies non-string mapping keys; distinct YAML keys can therefore collide after stringification and overwrite/lose information in the JSON representation
has no output truncation and no timeout; large documents can consume substantial memory or run without a time limit
safe_load accepts one document only and does not preserve comments, anchors, aliases, scalar styles, tags, key ordering guarantees across consumers, or original formatting

some safely constructed YAML values are not directly JSON-compatible, including timestamps/dates, binary values, sets, recursive aliases, or unsuitable mapping keys; emit then raises an uncaught serialization error
duplicate mapping keys are not explicitly rejected and may be overwritten according to PyYAML behavior
reads UTF-8 only, writes no JSON file, applies no application schema, and catches only yaml.YAMLError

output_contract.description: JSON envelope containing the single PyYAML safe_load value when JSON-serializable; default json.dumps allow_nan=true can leave NaN/Infinity non-strict RFC JSON, and non-string YAML keys are stringified with possible collisions, or a handled YAML parse error.

json_schema.description: Native JSON representation only; no field or task-delivery guarantee.

intent_tags: parse one YAML document into a JSON-compatible value
convert a local YAML configuration to JSON output
negative_intents: preserve YAML comments formatting or anchors
write a JSON file or validate an application schema
